n4176309638dc: Altermagnetism---moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting---has so far been realized primarily in N\'eel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g.,$\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[{C}_{2}||\mathcal{T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and the finite interchain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice ${C}_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.

n7ee6141fab85: Relaxation does not always reward patience: under certain conditions, a system initially farther from equilibrium can relax faster than one initially closer, a counterintuitive phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect. A conceptually transparent mechanism underlying this effect is the strong Mpemba effect, which commonly requires a unique slowest decay mode. However, for the Davies map, this condition is relaxed: the degenerate slowest modes are purely coherent. This allows the strong Mpemba effect to be realized by strategically eliminating coherence from the initial state. In this Letter, we design and implement a fully controllable optical setup to simulate the Davies map, whose validity is confirmed by verifying the semigroup property of the dynamics. We further demonstrate a genuine quantum strong Mpemba effect in the minimal quantum system, a single qubit. Our results experimentally confirm the key role of quantum coherence in this anomalous thermal relaxation. Moreover, our experimental setup provides a versatile platform for exploring quantum thermodynamics and a wider range of open-system dynamics.
n541a44199e6a: Achieving intrinsic Chern insulators (CIs) with zero net magnetization remains a long-standing and formidable challenge. Here, motivated by the unique opportunities that topological magnons offer for low-dissipation transport, we propose a general theoretical framework for realizing magnon CIs in filling-enforced fully compensated ferrimagnets with vanishing net magnetization. Moreover, we demonstrate that strong asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg interactions induce a type-III (broken-gap) magnonic band alignment, characterized by nonoverlapping magnon frequency gaps of the two layers, thereby enabling the emergence of magnon CIs. Remarkably, the asymmetric Bose-Einstein occupations of oppositely chiral magnon branches offer a distinct advantage in generating a giant magnon thermal Hall conductivity, which is forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets. Based on the Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model and first-principles calculations, we identify the experimentally accessible ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrGeTe}}_{3}$ and ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrSiTe}}_{3}$ heterostructures as ideal material platforms for realizing the proposed magnon CIs with fully compensated ferrimagnetism. These heterostructures host the nonzero magnon Chern numbers and chiral edge states, and remarkably display the strongly enhanced magnon thermal Hall effect comparable to that of ferromagnets, establishing fully compensated ferrimagnets as a promising platform for topological magnon transport without net magnetization.

n02653a75919c: Ultrafast light-driven chemical dynamics at surfaces are governed by energy transfer from excited electrons to vibrational degrees of freedom. When this nonadiabatic energy transfer is anisotropic, it can lead to dynamical steering effects that affect reaction probabilities or nonthermal final energy distributions in molecules. Here, enabled by a machine-learning-based simulation framework, we compare isotropic and anisotropic models of electronic friction during laser-driven hydrogen evolution on the (111) facet of copper. While anisotropic electronic friction determines the rate of energy transfer into the adsorbate and the fluence dependence of desorption probabilities, final translational, vibrational, and rotational energy distributions are mainly governed by the potential energy landscape at the barrier and insensitive to nonadiabatic effects.
n80e3b357e6bf: Systematic pulse-area errors limit the fidelity of quantum control across many qubit platforms. We introduce twinned dynamical decoupling, an analytic family of sequences $T2n$ in which a pulse sequence is paired with its $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase-shifted twin. This $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase step cancels common-mode systematic pulse-area errors to all orders on exact resonance. Then the phases of the pulses in each of the constituent twins are determined in such a manner that detuning errors are suppressed to the highest possible order as well. We have derived a simple analytic formula for these phases applicable to arbitrary sequence length. We demonstrate the sequences with superconducting transmon qubits on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_torino and the IQM Quantum processor Garnet. The measured population plateaus agree closely with theory and show enhanced robustness compared to the most frequently used dynamical decoupling protocols.

n1df7bc216a4f: Surface spin waves of the Damon-Eshbach type exhibit intrinsically nonreciprocal transport properties with a chiral dynamical field structure that localizes counterpropagating waves at opposite film surfaces. Such chirality has been predicted to suppress direct backscattering in thin films within frequency ranges free of bulk modes. However, how chirality influences reflection in thicker three-dimensional magnetic media, where a dense spectrum of bulk excitations overlaps with surface waves, remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that, in micrometer-thick yttrium iron garnet films, reflection of the chiral Damon-Eshbach wave from the boundary of the magnetic medium is accompanied by excitation of spatially localized thickness-quantized bulk modes, whereas reciprocal backward-volume waves reflect nearly elastically. Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, infrared thermography, and micromagnetic simulations reveal standing bulk excitations at the reflecting boundary and quantify the associated magnon energy accumulation and dissipation. These results identify bulk-mode excitations as the physical pathway enabling reversal of chirally localized surface waves in thick films, thereby defining the limits of chirality-based backscattering immunity and providing a general framework for wave transport in nonreciprocal magnetic media.
n56526304c817: Quasicrystalline Hamiltonians host Cantor-like spectra, gaps, and critical states, yet conventional finite-patch diagonalization is often compromised by spectral pollution: spurious eigenvalues absent from the infinite system. We introduce a certified spectral-computation framework for aperiodic media, computing infinite-volume spectra of general Hermitian Hamiltonians with rigorous a posteriori error bounds and without imposing artificial boundaries or artificial periodicity. The method resolves fine spectral features and fractal dimensions universally across aperiodic systems. For twisted Penrose bilayers, angle-resolved certified spectra identify a magic angle at $\ensuremath{\theta}\ensuremath{\approx}27.228\ifmmode^\circ\else\textdegree\fi{}$, where ring-worm interference produces twist-controlled confinement. Across one- and two-dimensional quasicrystals, the results show how fractal spectral geometry organizes localization: lower box-counting dimension correlates with larger inverse participation ratio in substitution chains, while dodecagonal tilings exhibit compactly supported and algebraically confined critical modes. The framework also scales to three dimensions, delivering contamination-free, high-resolution spectra for a quasicrystal arising in acoustic metamaterials. Further examples involving quantum walks, continuum superlattices, longer-range hopping, and inhomogeneous magnetic fields demonstrate the broad reach of certified spectral computation as a route to predictive spectral design in aperiodic media.
n7323001aca94: The $GW$ approximation is a cornerstone of many-body perturbation theory for computing single-particle excitations, yet it can fail qualitatively in strongly correlated systems where the single-reference picture becomes inadequate. To overcome this limitation, we develop a diagrammatic route to multireference $GW$ (MR-$GW$) from an interacting active-space reference, treating strong correlation nonperturbatively and the residual interaction through dynamical screening at the multireference random phase approximation level. Because the conventional diagrammatic self-energy expansion no longer applies, we define a practical one-shot MR-$GW$ approximation within a generalized diagrammatic framework, recovering standard $GW$ as a special case. Applications to prototypical correlated atoms and molecules show that the interacting active-space reference captures multiconfigurational satellite structures poorly described by single-reference $GW$, while dynamical screening generally improves the satellite energies as well as the leading ionization and electron-attachment energies. This work opens a diagrammatic route to Green's-function methods that combine nonperturbative strong correlation with dynamical screening.
